issues.legal_issue: Interim protection of a claimant’s possession may be granted while a dispute over possession and title remains pending adjudication.
material_facts: The applicants sought an interim injunction to prevent interference with their claimed possession of part of the land.
The parties disputed the applicants’ claim to the land, and the underlying suit remained to be tried.
The Court declined to assess the evidence finally because doing so could prejudice a fair trial, but held that this was not a case in which interim protection should be refused.
issues.conclusion: The respondents were restrained from interfering with the applicants’ possession of the suit land pending adjudication.
issues.legal_principle: When considering an interim injunction, a court may examine whether the applicant was at any time in lawful possession; if that is established prima facie, the opposing party may be asked to explain how the applicant was dispossessed. The court should avoid final findings on disputed evidence before trial where those findings could prejudice a fair decision. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited in the supplied judgment.

predicates.interim_possession_injunction_case: The proceeding seeks an interim injunction against interference with possession while a land dispute is pending.
predicates.claimant_seeks_protection_of_possession: The claimant asks the court to protect the claimant’s possession of disputed land.
predicates.possession_dispute_remains_for_trial: The parties’ dispute about possession remains unresolved and is to be examined at trial.
predicates.interim_possession_protection_should_be_: The claimant’s possession should be protected by an interim injunction pending adjudication.

issues.definition: When an interim possession injunction is sought and the possession dispute remains for trial, the rule calls for interim protection of the claimant’s possession.

issues.legal_issue: Interim restraint on use of development rights over disputed land is appropriate when construction may make the dispute irreversible and the restraint causes little inconvenience to the opposing party.
material_facts: The respondents were permitted to use development rights on the footing that they were entitled to construct over the whole plot, including the portion claimed by the applicants.
The Court considered that construction using those rights over the disputed portion could make the situation irreversible before the dispute was decided.
The respondents were in possession of about 9,000 square metres on which they could construct, so the restraint was not likely to inconvenience them.
issues.conclusion: The respondents were restrained from using development rights on the footing that they possessed the whole plot.
issues.legal_principle: In deciding whether to grant interim relief, the court considers where the balance of convenience lies and whether allowing the challenged conduct may create an irreversible situation before the dispute is resolved. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited in the supplied judgment.

predicates.interim_development_rights_injunction_ca: The proceeding seeks interim restraint on the use of development rights while a land dispute is pending.
predicates.disputed_land_included_in_construction_b: The opposing party’s asserted basis for construction includes land whose ownership or possession is disputed.
predicates.construction_may_make_dispute_irreversib: Construction before the dispute is decided may create a situation that cannot readily be reversed.
predicates.alternative_land_available_for_construct: The opposing party has other land available on which construction can proceed without using the disputed land.
predicates.use_of_development_rights_on_whole_land_: Use of development rights on the basis that the opposing party possesses the whole disputed area should be restrained pending adjudication.

issues.definition: When an interim proceeding concerns development rights over disputed land, construction may make the dispute irreversible, and other land remains available for construction, the rule calls for restraint on use of those rights over the whole land.
